description.description:
Located in the northeast corner of Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument, site of the 1980 eruption, the Mount Margaret Backcountry offers excellent backpacking opportunities. Eight designated campsites are scattered throughout the high-elevation lakes and jagged ridgelines of the remote area, offering a rugged hiking experience. Trails cross through forest that was blown down by the dramatic lateral blast of the eruption, leaving behind a scoured landscape that has since regenerated with young fir and alder trees, wildflowers and berry bushes. Although the trails are steep and challenging, the views of Mount St. Helens, Mount Rainier and the Cascade Range, as well as the quiet solitude, are unparalleled. 

The 110,000 acre Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument on the Gifford Pinchot National Forest was set aside by Congress in 1982 to protect significant features and the unique geologic, ecologic and cultural resources in the landscape surrounding the volcano. An important objective of the legislation is to allow geologic forces and ecological succession to operate substantially unimpeded by human activity. When visiting the Mount Margaret Backcountry, please support the Monument’s objectives by staying on trail, following regulations outlined on your permit and using the provided tent pad, grey water sump and toilet facilities. 

Mount St. Helens is just one of the many National Monuments that are part of our national heritage of public lands, offering a variety of recreation and scientific opportunities to both the local and global community. Our collective of volunteers, partners, scientists and employees help make this remarkable place a destination for visitors from around the world. We invite you to become part of this dedicated and vibrant community. We hope you will return and explore each of the three different sides of the Monument: the unmatched crater views and amazing landslide-filled valley on the West Side (State Route 504 to Johnston Ridge), the lava flows, volcanic mudflows and beautiful forests on the South Side (Forest Roads 90 and 83 to Ape Cave and Lava Canyon); and the amazing blown-down forests, standing dead forests and Spirit Lake views on the East Side (Forest Roads 25 and 99 to Windy Ridge). Enjoy your visit!
description.discounts: There are no discounts on Mount Margaret Backcountry camping permits.
description.driving_directions:
To the South Coldwater Trailhead (Late Spring to Summer Access):  

  • From I-5, take exit 49 toward Castle Rock/Toutle 
  • Follow WA-504 east for 42 miles, entering Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument 
  • Turn right, following signs for Coldwater Lake/Johnston Ridge Observatory 
  • Trailhead will be on the left  

To the Norway Pass Trailhead (Late-Summer Access):  

Summer of 2024 access to Norway Pass is only via Highway 12 due to a washout on Forest Road 25 south of Forest Road 99.

  • From I-5 take exit 68 east on Highway 12 to Randle
  • From Highway 12 turn right onto State Route 131
  • Continue on State Route 131 south until it be comes Forest Road 25
  • Continue on Forest Road 25 to Forest Road 99
  • Turn right onto Forest Road 99, following signs for Windy Ridge
  • Turn right onto Forest Road 26
  • Trailhead will be on the left
description.fee_policy:
Reservation Fee: $6.00 non-refundable fee. 

Recreation Fee: Overnight Mount Margaret Backcountry permits are $7.00 per person, per night, May 1st - November 30th.  

*The recreation fee finances on-the-ground administration and management of the Mount Margaret Backcountry Permit Area. Trailhead passes for parking are included in the permit cost for the duration of your overnight trip, and are part of your permit PDF. 

Day use visitors to Mount Margaret Backcountry are required to display a valid Recreation Day Pass, Northwest Forest Pass, or America the Beautiful Pass - available online, at the ranger station, or at the trailhead.
description.need_to_know_email:
Mount Margaret Backcountry Pre-trip Checklist:  

Give a copy of your itinerary to your emergency contact or trusted family member or friend. 

Print your permit within 14 days of your date of entry. Permits must be printed by 10 a.m. on the date of entry or the permit will be canceled. 

Review maps of the area and Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument. Plan contingency routes other than your primary route of travel. 

Identify reliable water sources and plan to treat all water for drinking. 

The backpacking season in the Mount Margaret Backcountry is short—expect to cross snowfields in spring and early summer, and the possibility of snow in the fall as well. 

Protect wildlife—pack and use a bear-resistant food canister, as most sites lack trees for hanging food. 

If you must cancel a reservation, cancel your permit as soon as you are able to allow other visitors to reserve the campsite. Changes to a reservation are allowed if made more than 7 days before the date of entry. Once a permit is printed, it cannot be cancelled or changed. Changes to the date of entry requires a new permit; cancel your existing permit and create a new reservation (a $6 nonrefundable reservation fee will apply).
description.need_to_know_order:

  • I understand that there are no refunds of the permit fee or reservation fee for cancellations or unfavorable weather conditions.

description.need_to_know_pdf:
General Permit Policy:

  • Permits are non-transferrable. If you are not able to use your permit, please cancel it in order to allow others the chance to reserve a site.

  • Permit holder must carry government-issued photo ID with permit and show it to Forest Service personnel upon request. Permits are not valid without ID.

  • Permit is not valid if trip is started on a date, or displayed in a site, other than what is indicated on the permit.

  • The maximum group size is 4, and at least one person per group must be at least 18 years of age.

Camping Regulations and Guidelines:

  • All overnight use in the Mount Margaret Backcountry requires a permit. Permits are only valid in the designated sites and dates listed on the permit.

  • A valid recreation pass (day pass, Northwest Forest Pass, America the Beautiful/Senior/Access Pass) is required when parking at the Norway Pass trailhead (http://www.discovernw.org/store_recreation-passes_1PASS/).

  • Campfires are not permitted in the Mount Margaret Backcountry—bring a backpacking stove.

  • Pack stock are not allowed.

  • It is illegal to cut any standing tree, dead or alive, damage vegetation, or damage any natural feature for any reason.

  • Camp only on the provided tent pads—do not camp on vegetation or near water.

  • Use the provided composting toilets. If a toilet is not available, dig a cat hole 6 to 8 inches deep at least 200 feet from water sources or campsites. When finished, fill hole and cover with soil. Pack out your toilet paper to reduce your impact further.

  • Treat all water by boiling, using purification tablets, or filtering.

Pets and Wildlife:

  • Dogs are permitted in the Mount Margaret Backcountry, but it is strongly encouraged that they be leashed to protect their safety and the safety of wildlife.

  • Carry and use a bear-resistant food canister—trees may not be available for hanging food.

  • Do not urinate within campsite areas. This encourages mountain goats, which are common in the area, to become habituated to human contact and may lead to abnormal and aggressive behaviors.

  • Prevent wild animals from becoming habituated to humans - enjoy them from a distance that is safe for both you and them. Never feed wildlife.

Emergency and Other Information:

  • In case of emergency, dial 911. However, do not rely only on your cell phone. Visitors are cautioned not to substitute a cell phone for adequate preparedness, such as carrying the Ten Essentials, leaving your itinerary with a trusted friend or family member and establishing a contingency plan.

  • The Mount Margaret Backcountry is an active ecological research area. Protect ongoing research by staying on trail, observing wildlife from a distance and leaving any research sites you may find undisturbed.
description.need_to_know_permit:
Conditions of Use: 

  • The person making the reservation is the permit holder. The permit holder must be 18 years or older. 

  • Permit holder must carry valid Government-issued photo ID while in the Mount Margaret Backcountry. 

  • A valid permit must be displayed on a tent while occupying the campsite. 

  • Maximum group size is 4 persons (8 persons for Ridge Camp)

  • Permit may be printed within 14 days of the date of entry. 

Rules and Regulations:

  • All overnight camping in the Mount Margaret Backcountry requires a valid permit. 

  • Never place garbage in the composting toilets; you must pack out all trash. 

  • Stock are not permitted. 

  • Fires are not permitted. 

  • Bicycles are not permitted, except on the Boundary Trail #1. 

  • The landing of drones or other aircraft in the MMBC is prohibited. 

  • If parking at the Norway Pass or Coldwater Trailhead, a valid recreation pass must be displayed.  Your permit includes two parking passes to be used in lieu of your recreation pass. 

Remember: 

  • Practice Leave No Trace ethics in all your outdoor activities.

  • Bear-resistant food canisters are recommended due to a lack of trees for hanging food. 

  • Give a copy of your itinerary to a trusted friend or relative in case of emergency. 

  • This area is often snow-bound until late spring or early summer. Snowdrifts often remain until July. Winter conditions arrive early in the fall as well. 

  • The Whittier Ridge Route #214 is particularly exposed and unmaintained, with steep drop-offs. Visitors uncomfortable with these conditions should choose alternative routes. 

  • Most trails in the MMBC are narrow in areas and rugged in design; trail conditions are best suited to experienced hikers and backpackers. 

  • Not all trailheads are open at all times of year. Permit holders are responsible for determining the status of roads within the Gifford Pinchot National Forest, either via the Gifford Pinchot National Forest webpage or by calling MSHNVM.

  • Call Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument, (360) 449-7800 or visit https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/giffordpinchot/recreation/mount-margaret-backcountry for current conditions.
description.no_show_policy: Permits must be printed by 10 a.m. on the date of entry or the permit will be cancelled.
description.quota_details: Camping is limited to 8 designated sites, with one permit issued per site per night (except Ridge Camp, which allows for 2 permits per night). Group size is limited to 4 persons per group, or up to 8 persons total at Ridge Camp.
description.season_information:
To protect natural resources and prevent crowding, permits are required for overnight camping in the Mount Margaret Backcountry between May 1st and November 30th. This area is often inaccessible due to snow until late spring or early summer and is not guaranteed to be accessible by May 1. Early season access is typically from the State Route 504 trailheads. Camping is only allowed at designated sites. Group size is limited to 4 persons per group (8 persons at Ridge Camp). A permit may be printed up to 14 days before your reservation date. Once your permit has been printed, you cannot make changes.  

If you cannot make your reservation, please cancel the reservation promptly to allow other persons the opportunity to visit.  

Permits are released in one month increments on the first day of the preceding month. For example, all May permits are released on April 1. All releases occur at 7:00 AM Pacific Time.

payload.directions: Visitors can access the Mount Margaret Backcountry from the north side of State Route 504 at the Coldwater Lake boat launch, South Coldwater Trail #230A or from Johnston Ridge Observatory at the end of State Route 504. Visitors also have access on the east side of the Mount Margaret Backcountry from the Norway Pass Trailhead, located on Forest Road 26.
